decisions.decision: Phase package copied into docs/phases/local-intelligence/package and fingerprinted, so the spec cannot drift silently and CI can read contracts/fixtures.
Runtime policy is computed from actual server configuration and exposed in /api/capabilities (runtime_policy); it authorizes nothing.
eval/src/v2/run.ts BudgetLedger(5) is historical; no phase model run may use it. Any LP24+ run needs a new ledger capped by the phase budget ($3.00 total).
Evaluator decisions carry evaluator=dk.aws_policy_eval.v2; access_paths schema id unchanged because the change is additive fields plus corrected classification, recorded here and in the receipt.
An omitted resource policy key is now unresolved (null = none). An omitted permission boundary keeps v1 meaning 'none'; exporters must send 'unknown' when unreadable (declared limit).

Recipe run contract bumped to dk.recipe_run.v2 and every recipe to @2 (meaning changed: obligations, kinds, paging). v1 recipes are retired, not kept runnable, because v1 reproduces the LP02 defects; stored case text that quotes @1 is unchanged.
Recipe budget unit is one search page or one coverage question (max 12). Running out produces partial/not_run obligations and outstanding continuations, never an implied answer.

Run provenance is project-level in projects.meta.local_run (no DB migration), validated against dk.local.run_provenance.v1, orthogonal to dataset_kind. Reference pack uses dataset_kind live + local_run.

Adopted world-plan and verification-receipt proposals as dk.local.*.v1 (proposal ids rejected until migrated). investigation-contract, conclusion and repair-plan proposals deferred to the packages that implement them.

Surface registry support stays the product-wide ceiling; per-asset capability tier is derived only from scoped receipts and capped by the ceiling. externally_verified receipts are rejected while EXT01 is deferred.

Adopted investigation-contract and conclusion proposals as dk.local.investigation_contract.v1 / dk.local.conclusion.v1 (proposal ids rejected), extended with typed obligation targets, derivation inputs digest, negative-claim requirements, closure prerequisites and an optional machine-checkable claim predicate.

Contracts are derived only from case scope, linked findings/events, declared asset kinds, applicable recipes and the versioned obligation catalog dk.obligation_catalog.v1. Revisions and the obligation ledger are append-only (DB triggers). Readers get an effective view with invalidations applied; writes record them as a new revision.

M2 is implemented on branch phase/li-m2 in a separate worktree while M1 runs on phase/local-intelligence; it is rebased and fast-forwarded onto phase/local-intelligence after all four packages are green (never force-pushed).

Jobs advance only on explicit analyst calls (no background worker, no model). Each unit commits deliveries, cursor and budget in one transaction; deliveries are unique per (channel, job, step, ref). Budget-cut steps are partial_budget (resumable) and keep the contract collecting.

A result planned under an earlier contract revision counts only when that obligation's target and (if interval-bound) the interval are unchanged since; decisions bump the revision without invalidating unrelated in-flight work.

Claim availability = delivered to the investigator through a contract channel (job step, packet page, inspection) under a contract revision with the same scope; packet/inspect reads append to that access log but change no case, contract, job or conclusion.

Packets never trim the uncertainty section (413 instead); counterevidence is ordered first; required records are individual omissions; machine_proved is never emitted and flagged narrative keeps a conclusion a draft pending human semantic review (EXT05, deferred).

Focused MCP profiles investigation-read / investigation-author are selected by DK_MCP_PROFILE at process start; the full toolset stays the default. Profile, project, output budget and per-call unit cap are fixed at start and no tool takes such an argument. Output envelope dk.mcp_envelope.v1. lab-request is not offered (no executor exists).

phase/li-m2 (LP08-LP11) rebased onto origin/phase/local-intelligence at 798f653 (M1 LP04-LP06). Conflicts: app.ts imports (kept both registerLocalWorld and registerInvestigationRoutes); STATUS.json merged automatically with every upstream package, requirement and decision entry preserved (checked by script). dk.local.scenario.v1 is a closed data format (14 typed actions, plain ids, declared route templates, single-segment params, unknown keys rejected at every level) validated twice: shape, then every reference against the compiled world. The engine executes only typed supervisor operations and hub faults.

Private truth (seed, labels, expectations, step records, tap-log effects) is a run-owned 0600 file in the run directory; the referee grades from truth + independent observers only; the investigator view is built solely from the DK API with a viewer token and leak-checked.

Scenario DSL documents stay in the repository for now; DK API/MCP/web are tested to have no path to them (source scan + static traversal test). Investigators with repo access are not blinded: such runs are development feedback, not held-out evaluation.

Browser-pilot failures on LP05/LP06 (and li-m2 run 40046522740) were a test timing race in e2e/redesign.spec.ts (baseline camera pose captured before a late overview refit). Fixed in the test by waiting for a stable pose and reading the baseline atomically with the Focus click; assertion unchanged.

The workbench is one read model (dk.case_workbench.v1) over existing M2 services and writes nothing; its packet is built with record:false so a person viewing it never makes a record 'available' to an agent's claim check.

Service principals (agents) may propose but cannot answer/settle case questions or hypotheses, remove items others added, or resolve/close a case (server-enforced 403). Proposals stay in investigation_conclusions with a per-case proposal_version and accepted:false.
Unsaved case drafts live in memory only, scoped to project+case+field, and are cleared with all sensitive client state; never written to web storage.

Analysis state elements are identified by (kind, authority, id): grants by AWS account + name within the account, artifacts by registry + asset:name. Addressing an element under another authority is refused, never resolved by name.

Candidates live only in append-only analysis_comparisons (namespace branch:<proposal digest>); comparisons are model_only and their receipt digest excludes timestamps so equal inputs give equal receipts.

A path hop is observed (and may animate) only when the relationship's own evidence level is observed with evidence refs; configured or conditional permission is never observed use, enforced on the server and again in the console.
Repair templates are a reviewed code constant (dk.repair_templates.v1), one per finite local action type; adding a template is a reviewed code change with tests, never runtime input.

Repair plans are plan_only and bound to the LP13 baseline and candidate state hashes; the authorization check only reports whether an approval descriptor still binds those digests and never authorizes execution. No apply/publish/PR route exists; patches are exported or materialised only in a fresh temp directory outside the checkout.

An objective needs at least one permitted operation (positive control); ranking uses only recorded criteria (validity, coverage, positive controls broken, unknowns, elements changed) and states it is not globally optimal.

The attention queue derives from the server's own project change stream (outbox) through a durable per-project cursor plus a bounded staleness scan; it never uses the R03.5 notifier or any remote destination. The only outbound path is an optional loopback-only test sink, off by default and checked at startup.

One item per (project, dedup_key); each distinct underlying record is an occurrence in the append-only attention_log, an identical record again only increments repeats. Acknowledgement accepts no fields beyond expected_seq, changes only the item, and a new distinct record reopens it.

Urgency is bounded: per-kind ceilings, never critical from local signals, repeats never raise it, and at most 5 items per project become high per hour (the rest are recorded medium with the reason). Items carry ids, counts and fixed template text only.
